purpose: 재첨부 V1 기준: 슬림한 체형 유지, 투구 장식 교체 및 갑옷의 입체 장식·볼륨·위압감 강화
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: SSS fantasy mercenary card illustration, portrait 2:3.
Input image 1 is the exact EDIT TARGET, reattached by the user. Follow this ornate version as the base. The user's correction is: keep the character SLIM and LUXURIOUS, redesign the HELMET ORNAMENTS, and give the ARMOR more three-dimensional ornament, volume and intimidating presence. The helmet and armor are the main design work.

Create a striking, lavish SSS imperial spear knight. This must be a visible upgrade in sculptural design and craftsmanship, not a simpler knight with fewer details.

HELMET:
Retain a fully enclosed, sharply tapered fantasy faceplate and slim head proportions. Replace the current few long curved horn blades with a sophisticated integrated imperial crown-helm ornament: layered openwork silver crestwork, strong angular architectural shapes with deep black recesses, and paired finely sculpted ornaments swept backward along the temples. Form an elegant regal silhouette with clearly composed central and side ornament, rather than three isolated flame horns. Put a small, deep amber-gold inset within a raised forehead setting. Use an imposing sculpted brow, narrow severe luminous eye slits and intricate overlapping silver cheek/face-guard contours. Fine engraved edges and restrained gold inlay enrich the crown and brow. The result should be threatening, aristocratic and exceptionally expensive, with ornament you can read immediately, even at card size. No human face, no plain bucket helmet, no simple horizontal visor, no skull mask. Helmet shell remains close to the head; ornament adds distinction without making the actual head huge.

ARMOR:
Keep the long-legged, slim adult knight, narrow waist and fitted limbs. Add depth and presence through SCULPTURAL ARMOR CONSTRUCTION. Make the pauldrons richer and more volumetric with tiered overlapping black-metal shells, raised silver ornamental ridges and carved relief panels; slightly fuller shoulders, but never a bulky body. Enrich the chest with a proud shaped breastplate, a prominent elegant central crest and interwoven raised silver contours standing above recessed dark metal. Fine warm-gold inlaid lines and small shadowed openings distinguish the layers. Give collar, upper arms, gauntlets, hip plates and greaves coordinated ornament. The upper chest and shoulder armor should feel commanding, ceremonial and formidable, with convincing plate thickness, bevels and cast shadows. Sculpted filigree and rich relief, not merely flat texture or tiny repeated scratches. Let polished silver catch the existing gold light against dark gunmetal. Keep the waist cinched, torso athletic, legs long and slender; create luxury and volume in the armor, not thick anatomy. Refined craftsmanship and a coherent hierarchy of large forms, medium relief and fine engraving.

LOCKED ELEMENTS:
Preserve the accepted shield and spear exactly in design, silhouette, size, location and grip; do not redesign, resize or simplify either. Keep the spear on its same straight rigid diagonal axis with its original ends. Preserve the full-body ivory-gold aura and its flowing ribbons, sparks and intensity from helmet to feet. Keep the same dark cathedral background, original framing, pose, hands, body proportions, mist and warm rim lighting. Armor and body stay opaque and readable through the aura. Preserve the polished painterly dark fantasy illustration style. Only redesign the helmet ornament and armor as requested.

Avoid: simplification, bland smooth armor, flattened decoration, generic medieval soldier, sci-fi bucket visor, chunky limbs, widened waist, oversized head, random spike clutter, all-gold armor, added wings or cape, extra weapons, extra limbs, changed shield/spear, new background. No lettering, rank text, card frame, logo or watermark.
